midnight-violet.$description: Midnight Violet — Dark section backgrounds, primary text on light surfaces, nav text — the deep brand violet anchors identity and gives the dark hero/sections their weight

lavender-whisper.$description: Lavender Whisper — Brand-tinted shadow, soft accent washes, subtle elevation glow — replaces neutral gray shadows so elevation stays on-brand

ghost-lilac.$description: Ghost Lilac — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

cornflower-pop.$description: Cornflower Pop — Rare accent for highlighted CTAs or featured buttons — a brighter blue-violet used sparingly for emphasis

cream-glow.$description: Cream Glow — Decorative pastel surface — soft yellow wash for feature cards or playful callouts against the violet system

blush-mist.$description: Blush Mist — Decorative pastel surface — pale pink wash for feature cards or playful callouts within the light sections

emerald-mint.$description: Emerald Mint — Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

cloud-canvas.$description: Cloud Canvas — Page canvas, light card surfaces, button text on dark — the near-white base that everything sits on

charcoal-ink.$description: Charcoal Ink — Primary text on light surfaces, text on cream/blush accents — the dark reading color

frost-white.$description: Frost White — Secondary light surface, subtle panel backgrounds, light section fills — a warm-tinted off-white for elevation

ash-veil.$description: Ash Veil — Tertiary surface, hairline borders, disabled states — barely-there gray for structural separation

slate-mute.$description: Slate Mute — Muted helper text, secondary icons, inactive nav items — mid-gray for de-emphasized content

phantom.$description: The sole typeface — custom Phantom with two whisper-light weights. Weight 350 for display/headlines, 400 for body and UI text. The single-weight light approach is anti-convention for crypto (which defaults to bold 700 headlines); the thin strokes make Phantom feel editorial and calm, not aggressive or financial. The custom letterforms — visible in the rounded 'a' and open 'e' — give the brand a distinctive typographic fingerprint that no system font replicates.
